speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing your history. Given your gait and limb ataxia, I need to determine if this is acute or progressive. Has your balance or coordination worsened over the past few weeks, or was there a sudden onset?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for clarifying; the "drunk" appearance and right-sided clumsiness suggest a focal neurological issue. To differentiate between a cerebellar stroke, a tumor, or a demyelinating event, can you describe if you experienced any sudden onset of weakness or numbness on the right side? REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vital Signs are Normothermic, Within normal range for Blood Pressure, Heart Rate, and Respiratory Rate. Neurological Examination reveals an Ataxic gait, Right Upper Limb Strength of 4/5, and Evidence of ataxia on Coordination Tests. MRI Brain findings show multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML).

speaker: Patient
text:
I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for mentioning Crohn's disease and natalizumab; this medication is known to increase the risk of progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML), but given your specific history and current presentation, I must prioritize ruling out a demyelinating flare. Has your vision changed recently, such as experiencing double vision or loss of color perception? REQUEST TEST: Ophthalmologic Exam and Visual Evoked Potentials.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your vision and evoked potentials are normal, we must investigate other causes of your ataxia. Given your history of Crohn's disease and natalizumab use, has your coordination worsened over the past few weeks, or was the onset sudden? REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast focusing on cerebellum and brainstem.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain with contrast focusing on cerebellum and brainstem findings show multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, consistent with Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML).

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy. The MRI findings of multifocal demyelinating lesions without enhancement, combined with your history of Crohn's disease and natalizumab use, confirm this opportunistic infection. We must discontinue natalizumab immediately and consider initiation of rituximab or ocrelizumab.
